standard-dialogue.npc: I think that Ur-tag is trying to move too quickly. First, he opens the city to humans, and now he wants to invite these dwarves into the city. I think we should exercise more caution in dealing with surface-dwellers.

standard-dialogue.speaker: Ur-taal
standard-dialogue.text: The dwarves are not surface dwellers. They live in an underground city, like us!

standard-dialogue.npc: Why does that mean we can trust them? Are you forgetting the machine that nearly destroyed us was made by dwarves?

standard-dialogue.speaker: Ur-taal
standard-dialogue.text: You shouldn't judge all dwarves because of that!

standard-dialogue.npc: I know that! And I know not all humans want to kill us, but I still never thought we should open the city.

standard-dialogue.speaker: Ur-taal
standard-dialogue.text: You can't deny it's done some good. Think of how happy everyone is trying surface foods in the market!

standard-dialogue.npc: I'm not denying that, I just don't think it's worth the risk. Our guards have their work cut out as it is, protecting us from renegade humans, without having to worry about dwarves as well.

standard-dialogue.speaker: Ur-taal
standard-dialogue.text: Please don't be offended by my friend's attitude, surface-dweller. I'm sure you understand why we need to be cautious.

options.text: Ask for permission to sell food in the market

steps.player: May I have permission to sell food in the market?
